<reflection>
Product experiment: M2, M6, M8, M18 still lead. M12 and M11 fit worse now, suggesting product inhibition (M12) and substrate deactivation (M11) are less likely. M4, M5, M9 also fit worse. Leaders M2 (dimerization equilibrium), M6 (cat activation), M8 (ligand equilibrium), M18 (2catS deactivation) share features around catalyst state.

Need to discriminate:
- M2 (dimer resting state): rate should be less than linear in [cat] at high cat
- M6 (cat→cat* irreversible activation): induction period, rate proportional to [cat]
- M8 (cat↔cat*+L): reversible activation, different kinetics
- M18 (2catS→inactive): bimolecular deactivation of catS species

M18 predicts strong deactivation at high catalyst; M2 predicts slower rate per cat at high loading (but reversibly). M6 predicts induction period.

Test at very high catalyst with low substrate - should amplify catalyst-catalyst interactions.
Actually, better test: low catalyst, long time - can we reach full conversion? M18 would still allow full conversion if S is limiting and cat regenerates from catS. Actually M18 destroys catS irreversibly.

Best discriminator: very low catalyst extends time - if M18/M13/M19, we see plateau. If M2, M6, M8, still full conversion.

Alternative: examine early-time behavior with high catalyst to see induction period (M6).
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
Test at high catalyst with moderate substrate to amplify differences:
- M2 (dimer equilibrium): [cat] appears less effective as dimer forms; rate ~ scales sub-linearly with cat
- M6 (irreversible activation): induction period, but with high cat, activation is complete quickly; final rate scales with cat
- M8 (cat↔cat*+L): equilibrium shifts as cat added; sub-linear scaling
- M18 (2catS→inactive): more deactivation at high cat, likely plateau below full conversion

At [cat]=0.05, [S]=0.5, [P]=0:
- M2: rate/cat lower than at cat=0.01
- M6: similar rate/cat as cat=0.01 (activation is fast)
- M8: rate/cat lower than at cat=0.01 (equilibrium)
- M18: plateau below full conversion (final [P] < 0.5)

Also, using lower substrate concentration will let us see whether reaction goes to completion.
</hypothesis>
